title: Token / server mode: one refresh per refresh token in a client family
caption: A third-party server derives two request clients for one visitor from its root client (withOptions({ accessToken: A1, refreshToken: R1, endUser })). Both calls get 401 TOKEN_EXPIRED; the family sends ONE POST /v1/auth/refresh with R1 and the API key only, records R1 → (A2, R2), reports the new pair once, and both calls are sent again with A2. internal/session.js refreshTokens, startRefresh, runRefresh, resolveRefresh.

steps.label: bookings.list({}) with A1 / R1 (same visitor, concurrent)
GET /v1/account  X-Api-Key: sk_…  Authorization: Bearer A1
resolveRefresh(R1): no rotation recorded → refreshing.get(R1) empty → startRefresh
POST /v1/auth/refresh { refreshToken: R1 } with the API key, host and endUser only (never A1)
refreshing.get(R1) → joins the same promise (holds the new token from now)
200 AuthSessionResult { session: { accessToken: A2, refreshToken: R2, … } }
steps.note: API side: customer_sessions row of R1 gets rotated_at / replaced_by_id; a new row holds hash(R2) in the same family_id.

steps.label: onSessionRefreshed(session with A2/R2): write the httpOnly cookies (awaited, errors ignored)
GET /v1/bookings again with Bearer A2 (no second refresh)
11 s later a late request still carries R1 in a token function
steps.note: Outside the 10 s rotation window and not held as the client's own string: R1 is sent as it is, the API answers 401 REFRESH_TOKEN_REUSED and revokes the whole family (the newest A2/R2 stop working too). That is deliberate: a stolen rotated token trips reuse detection.
